description: Autumn air: melancholic, cool and clear – records like a breath through falling leaves.
Chanson and French flair: café atmosphere – accordion, Gitanes, a croissant for the ears.
Sixty minutes of time travel: two songs per decade, as a pair – mainstream and underground, hit and answer.
Reverberant, drifting soundscapes – ambient to float away to.
The computer sets the beat – not mechanical, but like a real, pulsing heart.
Genre slot: hazy, guitar-led pop – dream images with tremolo.
A straight electronic hour: beats without distraction – one pulse, no detours.
Playground for the avant-garde: unheard sound ideas – the echo nobody expected.
Rock from as many countries as possible – geography over genre, border stone by border stone.
The guitarists' hour: solos, riffs, legends – from the blues lick to the feedback cathedral.
Slow, sprawling tracks – soul, dub, long fades. Longing for a home you knew – or never quite knew – carries the ride; arrival is beside the point.
Live recordings with a cheering crowd – the stage on air.
Slow, sprawling tracks – soul, dub, long fades. No hurry: the way home is the point, not the arrival.
One album, its songs and its friends: a record as the common thread – B-sides, guests, kindred tracks.
Your open drift hour – listener requests are inspiration, not a genre filter.
World news read calmly – with records in between that keep the pace steady.
Music as a flight: a take-off and a landing track per country – listeners' countries welcome on the route.
Long-form ambient, minimal talk, nothing sudden – for listeners falling asleep or working the night shift.
A ride on the groove: rhythm before melody, listener wishes as destinations – every stop a different beat.
Raw basement rock: unpolished, loud, direct – no stage, no shine.
Intimate recordings with room sound: small rooms, close mics – the walls quietly sing along.
The weekend disco party: four-on-the-floor, glitter, falsetto, funk and pop-rock from the 60s to the 80s.
Genre slot shoegaze: wall of guitars, veiled vocals – shine through fog, not polish.
Slowing down: only music under 100 BPM – the afternoon slides gently into evening light.
A gentle landing: warm, quiet music, sometimes classical.
Classical music for Sunday, relaxed and curated – the concert without a dress code.
Genre slot downtempo: fat samples, creaking beats, Bristol darkness – the slow beat for deep hours.
Weather report from listeners' regions with music that quotes the weather – and may turn like a front coming in.
A world-music journey: one continent after another – a leisurely walk, not a flight.
Big line-ups – not just orchestras but big bands too. A full stage: horns, choirs, strings or simply many musicians at once.
A stormy, loud hour – chaos with a system. Pure energy, unleashed under control.
A European brunch: music from the continent, served like a late breakfast – relaxed, varied, borderless.
Music for expats, quietly calling home. Wistfulness as a programme: memories of distant places, without pathos.
Fine, expensive soul – suit-and-sneakers vibe. Behind the velvet rope: soul for the penthouse and the underground alike.
Tracks over six minutes, uncut: 12-inch, extended, album cuts. Here time is made, not saved.
A weekly rotation through American roots music – each week a different branch (see this week's theme).
One instrument in the spotlight (like the harmonica in 'Once Upon a Time in the West') or spectacular solos.
80s neon nostalgia: synths, cassettes, city nights – a neon era rewound into the present.
Chance finds: records caught while digging through the library – whatever sticks gets played.
Dark and organic, with bass and dense atmosphere – ambient under tension.
Pop & rock songs from around the world in 20 songs – songs first, not just beats.
Alternative & indie: across the globe in 20 songs.
Heavy, warm bass, a strong pulse – driving and rocky, with an edge and temper.
Ancient roots of the moor dissolving into the light of the horizon: Celtic roots growing towards the light.
Old blues from the crossroads and the river: songs about roads, water and second chances.
Country-folk, bluegrass harmonies and gospel ground – the soil US rock grew from.
Where the streets still remember: son, tango and samba from the root – Latin American roads as memory.
Emotional charge, full of heart and inner tension – rocky and fiery.
The room is the instrument (cathedral, plate, spring, canyon reverb).
The original steps back behind the cover – covers that outshine the first version.
Music from Asia for the dinner slot.
City-night soundtrack: through the neon in a cab.
Film music and cinematic-sounding tracks.
Music that lets the end arrive – songs of farewell.
Forgotten records from the back of the shelf.
Indie anthems that give you goosebumps.
Lo-fi bedroom productions with art-pop ambition.
Grunge riffs with a danceable groove underneath.
Energy flows, the pulse is there – present and rocky.
No hard beats; fine electronic threads in the background, woven elegantly around acoustic instruments.
Melancholic, sunny summer mood.
Latin American rhythms (latido = heartbeat).
Cover versions and quotations.
A weekly ride through Europe's music – each week a different carriage (see this week's theme).
Funk, soul, groove – the republic of the danceable.
Genre slot: pop melodies on an ambient bed.
Current and classic music from Africa.
Smoky indie with a beat: close to the mic, hazy and slowly pulsing – à la Cigarettes After Sex.
Musical weather at the blue hour: cool twilight, muted colours – and the day announcing itself on the horizon.
Dark with bass – glowing, pressure with dangerous tension.
Music for the sunrises happening somewhere right now.
Studio intimacy: down to close-up volume.
Precision matters – timing, exactness, clockwork.
Yacht rock and smooth West Coast sound.
Songs under 2:30.
Soul for cooking: warm kitchen, warm grooves.
The hour of great voices – vocals at the centre.
Hip-hop from every hemisphere – not just the US.
Genre crossover: styles that collide.
Americana, taken easy – brunch time.
Genre slot: instrumental, building post-rock.
Weight and groove with rocky pressure – solid, gripping and driving.
Music from the time zones where it is already light.
Deliberate digital errors, dropouts, chopped vocals – arranged into a poetry of their own.
An uplifting hour: lightness to start the weekend.
Loud music as if it were night – in the middle of the day.
Listener participation: dedications, voices, listening.
Disco classics and nu-disco in the glitter light.
Genre slot: indie folk – fingerpicking, harmonies.
Spiritual currents on the weekend.
Improvisation vibe: live jams, long takes.
Music from exile: artists far from home, sounds that echo across borders.
Flow with bass and melancholy – surf and an electric edge, rocky and under tension.
Burnt out and heavy, weary grunge – ash, residual warmth and a last rocky echo.
Electronic sounds that grow and branch out: bright, fresh and alive.
Genre-hopping mix of songs that don't belong together but somehow do.
Lonely nights, Ella and Coltrane at the bar, and neon flashing on the brass.
From the Beatles to trip-hop: British rock and pop history.
Piaf, Grönemeyer, Conte – Europe telling stories in its own languages.
Glitter, Grand Prix and dancefloor anthems – from ABBA to Måneskin.
Kraftwerk, New Order, Daft Punk, Björk – Europe plugged in.

Soul has addresses: Detroit, Memphis, Philly, Chicago, London – a trip through the streets and churches it came from. From Motown and Stax to neo-soul; especially the songs in the shadow of the big hits.
One voice, one guitar and plenty of air: singer-songwriters and folk from around the world – from Nick Drake and Joni Mitchell to songs in other languages.
An invisible field around the Earth: electronic music from every continent – from Kraftwerk and Yellow Magic Orchestra to voices from countries rarely heard in electronic music.
Halloween hour: chills, goosebumps and gothic – from Thriller to Spellbound, with a wink.
A birthday ride through big band, swing revival and electro swing.
